summary: Puzzle Adventure tutorial step: builds a pickup key Blueprint (BP_Key) whose shape and color come from an Enum + Struct + Map variable, a Blueprint Function Library function that sets mesh/material, and a Blueprint Interface (BPI_PlayerKeys) so the player character stores collected keys on overlap. Also covers making a parameterized color material with Material Instances and swapping the Default Pawn Class.
gotchas: Pick the Cube/Sphere meshes from /Engine/BasicShapes or keys appear too large
Set the key mesh Collision Presets to NoCollision so only the capsule detects the player
Change a new Map element's key before adding another; duplicate keys can't be added
Interface functions without outputs act as events; ones with outputs are regular functions

summary: Puzzle Adventure tutorial step: modifies the first-person template's BP_DoorFrame so its Construction Script tints the door to match a RequiredKey, and adds an fnHasKey function (interface message + Array Contains) so the door's ActorBeginOverlap only plays Door Control when the player holds the matching key. Also shows Blueprint comment boxes, Print String debugging and execution tracing.
gotchas: Doors still open for NPCs or actors without BPI_PlayerKeys by design
Pasted Construction Script snippet needs an extra Sequence pin wired to the Branch
Print String messages don't display in a final game
Requires BP_Key, BPL_FPGame and BPI_PlayerKeys from the previous part

summary: Builds a UMG HUD widget (WBP_PlayerHUD) with Canvas Panel, Overlay, Vertical/Horizontal Boxes, Text, a multi-line Text Box and Background Blur, plus an fnAddKeyHUD function that lists collected keys; then creates the widget on Event Possessed in the character and adds it to the viewport. Ends with HUD readability design tips.
gotchas: Large Background Blur strengths cost more GPU; Border or Image widgets are cheaper
When overriding Event Possessed, use Add Call To Parent Function so parent logic still runs
SetText (Multi-Line Text Box) may need Context Sensitive disabled to find
Use a Text widget for labels, not a Text Box

summary: Builds a pressure-plate BP_Switch (box trigger, On/Off materials, emissive material, ActivateOnce flag, Get Overlapping Actors check) and a physics-simulating BP_Cube that can hold it down, then a BPI_Interaction interface with fnBPISwitchOn/Off that the switch broadcasts to an InteractObjectList actor array. Opens with game-design notes on difficulty, consequences and win conditions.
gotchas: EndOverlap turns the switch off while another actor is still on it unless you check Get Overlapping Actors
Trigger uses Custom collision: Query and Physics, WorldDynamic, WorldDynamic set to Ignore
Use Playmode > Current Camera Location to start PIE where the viewport is

summary: Builds BP_Platform that moves between its start location and a Target Point actor using a Timeline float track driving Lerp (Vector) into Set World Location, with custom events for forward/backward/stop, a WaitDuration Delay, Set Play Rate for speed (TimeToTarget), and BPI_Interaction events so a switch activates it. Also tunes physics cube Linear/Angular Damping so it stays on the platform.
gotchas: Use Add Timeline, not Add Timeline Component
Timeline is 1 s long, so farther target points mean faster platforms unless play rate is scaled
A fast platform throws physics cubes off; add damping and slow it
Set Play Rate may need Context Sensitive unchecked to find

summary: Creates a parent BP_TrapBase that calls Apply Damage on overlapping Characters via a looping Set Timer by Function Name (paused/unpaused on overlap), child spike and fire traps (fire trap toggled by BPI_Interaction), updates the HUD HP text from Event AnyDamage, and adds a game-over widget that disables input, waits, and reloads the level with Open Level.
gotchas: Function Name in Set Timer by Function Name must be spelled exactly or nothing runs
Timers start immediately when created; pause them until needed
Use Do Once before game-over logic since the player can keep being hit at 0 HP
Inherited variables aren't shown in a child's My Blueprint panel; set them in the graph or Construction Script
